title: Client traffic gate and rollback primitives for staged model promotion
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: Platform customers need a safe, auditable client-side surface for staged model promotions (canary/A-B/shadow) that guarantees idempotent control-plane operations, least-privilege permissioning, and deterministic auto-rollback behavior when quality or latency regressions are detected.

Goal: Add a compact set of SDK & control-plane primitives that enable product code to: 1) open a traffic gate for a new model variant with an idempotency token and explicit scope, 2) attach shadow routes for silent comparison, 3) exercise canary splits with time windows and ramp policies, and 4) trigger policy-driven automatic rollback with a recoverable audit trail. The work must include client helpers, API changes, end-to-end tests, and docs for developers and SREs.
implementation_notes: Idempotency: use a client-provided idempotency_key header that is checked against a rollbacks/reconciler ledger for 72 hours; ops can query by key.
Permission model: introduce 'traffic.gate.create' and 'traffic.gate.modify' granular scopes; SDK helpers will surface permission errors with remediation links.
Auto-rollback: tie to evaluation hooks (latency_percentile, regression_count, error_rate_windows) with configurable thresholds per deployment.
Shadowing: default shadow calls are sandboxed and billed separately; include opt-in flag to duplicate telemetry to customer-provided eval endpoints.
Consistency: control-plane returns a stable 'promotion_id' used for idempotent mutation and for correlating telemetry across systems.
tasks: Design API endpoints and protobufs for /v1/promotions and /v1/promotions/{id}/actions
Implement SDK helpers: TrafficGate.create(), TrafficGate.updateSplit(), TrafficGate.attachShadow()
Server: reconcile loop to enforce idempotency and crash-safe rollbacks
Permissions: add new scopes to authz service and map to console RBAC roles
E2E tests: simulate canary regressions (latency and quality) and assert auto-rollback
Docs: Quickstart, API reference, and runbook for on-call SREs
Security review and threat model for idempotency ledger and audit logs
Performance test: load test 50k small promotions/day to validate reconciler throughput
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes TrafficGate primitives with idempotency_key support and clear error classes
API supports creating promotions with shadow and canary routing options and returns promotion_id
Auto-rollback triggers predictably under synthetic regression signals and creates an audit event
Permission checks prevent lower-privilege users from opening production traffic gates; console shows actionable error
End-to-end tests pass in staging and we have a runbook with rollback verification steps
Monitoring: dashboards show promotion counts, rollback counts, and reconciler lag under 30s
updates: 2026-02-20: Initial ticket created after design spike with PM and SRE. Agreed scope for canary/shadow/rollback primitives.
2026-02-24: API sketch reviewed with backend; added promotion_id and idempotency_key fields to the model. Kept the promotion lifecycle states minimal (pending, active, paused, rolled_back, archived).

2026-02-27: SDK contract v0.1 implemented in typescript and python; basic create/update flows work against staging control-plane. Observed race when two clients reuse same idempotency_key concurrently; reconciler patch landed to serialize by key.
2026-03-01: Permission scopes drafted; security review kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-04. E2E test harness populated with synthetic latency/quality signals.
comments: Sofia Patel (PM): Please ensure the SDK surfaces both immediate errors and eventual reconciliation status so clients can show a deterministic UI state.
Marcus Liu (SRE): Reconciler must expose metrics for in-flight promotions; we hit 120s delays in a previous experiment and need sub-30s SLO.
Rohit Singh (Auth): We'll add 'traffic.gate.*' permissions to the RBAC matrix; need final list of API verbs before policy rollout.
Ava Kim (Assignee): Implemented naive ledger + lock-based serialization. Next: replace with reconciler-backed idempotency table and soft-ttl to avoid indefinite locks.
notes_for_review: Design trade-off: server-side reconciler vs immediate strong locks. Chose reconciler for availability but added short lease to reduce duplicate work.
Privacy: shadow traffic payloads are redacted by default; customer can opt-in to forward raw payloads to their eval endpoint (documented).
Edge-case: if promotion_id is archived, any idempotent retry must return a 409 with guidance to create a fresh promotion.
